title: How to Build Financial Agents That Work Across the Web - Jay Sahnan & Arik Bird, Browserbase
talk_summary: Browserbase pitches hosted, fingerprinted Chromium plus the Stage Hand SDK so agents can drive arbitrary websites without hand-written Playwright selectors. The one genuinely transferable engineering idea is shrinking raw HTML into a compact accessibility-tree representation before sending it to an LLM, cutting token cost and latency.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of passing raw HTML to the model, they reduce the page to a compact accessibility tree with direct selectors, then send that to the LLM to decide where to click.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it shrinks the DOM to a really cool accessibility tree, where we're only sending like 4,000 tokens for this same example
takeaways.numbers: 122k tokens raw HTML vs ~4k tokens compressed for the same page

takeaways.what_they_do: Stage Hand exposes act/observe/extract primitives: deterministic Playwright-style calls for stable steps, LLM-driven natural-language actions only when the page is complex or changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can use deterministic rules and go page.click ... But, when it gets a little bit more complex, you can actually send natural language prompts

takeaways.technique: Keep browser process alive across tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than killing Chromium after each job, they leave the process running and just close windows, avoiding cold-start cost per task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead, we leave chromium running and close the windows out.
